sync.headline: One catalog, two channels
sync.description: Your WooCommerce products are your POS products. Update a price or stock level once — it syncs everywhere automatically. No manual entry, no conflicts, no guesswork.

offline.headline: Works offline
offline.description: Local-first architecture means the POS keeps running when your connection drops. Products are stored locally and open orders are preserved — they complete and sync as soon as the internet returns.

hardware.description: Native iOS and Android apps — not a browser tab pretending to be an app. Connect payment terminals, receipt printers, and barcode scanners directly.

ownership.description: Your data stays in your WooCommerce store, on your hosting. No platform lock-in, no third party holding your business hostage. Open source (GPL) — inspect the code, extend it, contribute to it.

freePlugin.question: Is the free plugin limited?
freePlugin.answer: No. The free WCPOS plugin is GPL software with full point of sale features — unlimited products, orders, and customers, and no transaction fees. Pro adds the advanced tools listed above.

yearlyVsLifetime.question: What's the difference between Yearly and Lifetime?
yearlyVsLifetime.answer: The Yearly license is a one-time payment that includes updates and priority support for one year. It does not renew automatically. The Lifetime license is a one-time payment that includes updates forever.

expiry.question: What happens when my license expires?
expiry.answer: Nothing switches off. The Pro version you already have keeps working — your register, your data, every feature. What stops is new updates and priority support, until you choose to renew. That is deliberate: renewals have to be earned with updates worth paying for, and it means your point of sale can never be disabled remotely.

This policy explains what personal data we collect when you use the site, why we collect it, who processes it on our behalf, and what rights you have over it. We aim to collect as little as we need to run the service.

c1.label: Account information.
c1.body: Your email address and name when you create an account, either directly or by signing in with Google, GitHub, or Discord. When you use a sign-in provider, we receive only your basic profile (email, name or username, and avatar or picture URL) from that provider, and may store the avatar or picture URL on your account as oauth_avatar_url.

c2.label: Billing details.
c2.body: The billing address and any company details you enter at checkout, stored with your customer record so we can issue receipts and comply with tax rules.

c3.label: Order and license history.
c3.body: Records of your purchases, license keys, and plugin downloads, so you can manage your licenses and we can provide support.

c4.label: Payment information.
c4.body: Payments are handled by Stripe and PayPal. Your full card number or payment credentials never reach our servers; we receive only a payment confirmation and the details needed for the receipt.

c5.label: Usage analytics.
c5.body: We use PostHog to understand how the site is used (pages viewed, buttons clicked). To do this, we set a cookie containing a randomly generated identifier. It does not contain your name or email.

c6.label: Error reports.
c6.body: If something breaks, an error report may be sent to Sentry. Reports can include technical details such as your browser and operating system and what the application was doing at the time of the error.

c7.label: Server logs.
c7.body: Our servers keep application logs (in Grafana Loki) for debugging and operating the service.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.body: We use a small number of first-party cookies. We do not use third-party advertising cookies.

items.k1: medusa-token — keeps you signed in to your account. Expires after 1 day.
items.k2: wcpos-analytics-consent — remembers your analytics consent choice (accepted or declined). Expires after 182 days.
items.k3: wcpos-distinct-id — a random identifier used for analytics. Only set after you accept analytics on the consent banner; removed if you decline. Expires after 1 year.
items.k5: Your light/dark theme preference is stored locally in your browser and is never sent to us.

processors.title: Who processes your data
processors.body: We use the following service providers to run wcpos.com. Each receives only the data needed for its role:

p1.label: Our commerce backend (Medusa)
p1.body: — self-hosted on Hetzner infrastructure in the EU. Stores accounts, customer records, and orders.

p4.label: Keygen
p4.body: — software license management (license keys and activations).

items.r1: Account and license data is kept while your account is active. If you ask us to delete your account, we delete it, except where we are legally required to keep records.
items.r2: Order and invoice records are kept for as long as tax and accounting laws require.
items.r3: The analytics identifier cookie expires after 1 year.
items.r4: Server logs and error reports are kept for a limited operational window and then deleted.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.body: If you are in the EU/EEA or UK, you have rights under the GDPR, including the right to access, correct, delete, and export your personal data, and to object to or restrict certain processing. We extend the same rights to all users regardless of location.
rights.exercise: To exercise any of these rights, email us at <email>support@wcpos.com</email> so we can verify your identity privately. EU/EEA residents also have the right to lodge a complaint with their local data protection authority.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
changes.body: If we make material changes to this policy, we will update the date at the top of this page. Continued use of the site after a change means the updated policy applies.

refunds.title: Refund Policy
refunds.intro: WCPOS Pro is downloadable software. The moment you buy, you have the license key and the files — there is nothing to hand back. So we don’t run a no-questions-asked money-back window: the free version is the trial, and it never expires. What we offer instead is more useful — if WCPOS Pro doesn’t do what we say it does, we will fix it or refund you.

prevention.lead: The free version is the trial version. The full point of sale — unlimited products, orders and customers — runs on your store for as long as you like, at no cost and with nothing to cancel. Everything else you need to judge Pro is public too, so please use it before you pay.

yes.lead: Email us and we will put it right if:

items.y1: WCPOS Pro doesn’t do something this website, the documentation, or our answer to a pre-sale question said it does.
items.y2: A bug or an incompatibility stops you using a Pro feature, and we can’t fix it within a reasonable time.
items.y3: Something went wrong with the purchase itself — you were charged twice, charged the wrong amount, or never received a working license key.

no.title: When we don’t

items.n1: You changed your mind, or bought without checking whether WCPOS Pro suits the way your store runs.
items.n2: You want a feature we never claimed to have. Ask before you buy — we answer honestly, including when the answer is no.
items.n3: The cause is in your hosting, your theme, or another plugin, and we aren’t given what we need to diagnose it.

no.note: This describes when we use our own discretion. It does not affect your legal rights, which are set out below and which we honour in full.

items.p1: A Pro license buys a year of updates and priority support — not permission to run the software. When it expires nothing switches off: your register, your data and every Pro feature keep working exactly as before. That is deliberate. A point of sale that can be disabled remotely is one that can fail you mid-trade, and I am not willing to build that.
items.p2: Renewing is a decision too, never an automatic charge. No card is kept on file, and nothing bills you again unless you choose to buy again. It is the fairest arrangement I could come up with, and it cuts both ways: if I stop shipping updates worth paying for, you simply don’t renew — which is exactly the pressure I want to be under.
items.p3: There is a flip side, and I would rather say it plainly. Once Pro is installed and activated it keeps running whether or not the license behind it is current. Refunding a purchase revokes the key, which ends updates and support, but it does not reach into your site and take anything back. That part of the arrangement runs on good faith — and nearly everyone honours it.
items.p4: WCPOS is built by one person. The free plugin is open source and always will be, and Pro is what pays for the time that goes into both. A refund is not a neutral reset: the card fees are spent either way, and so are the hours that went into pre-sale questions and helping set a store up.
items.p5: So the ask is simple. Try it first — the free version is right there, the demo runs the current Pro build, and I answer pre-sale questions honestly, including when the answer is no. Do that, and if Pro still doesn’t do what I said it would, you get your money back without an argument. What I can’t carry is refunding people who bought without looking.

request.body: Email <email>support@wcpos.com</email> from the address you bought with, and tell us what WCPOS Pro is not doing. Give us the chance to fix it first — most requests turn out to be a setting or a bug we can resolve quickly. If we can’t, we refund you.

payment.title: How refunds are paid

Bitcoin payments are refunded by arrangement — email us and we will agree the method with you. A refunded license key is revoked and stops working immediately.

renewals.body: Yearly licenses never renew automatically, so there is no surprise charge to reverse — we cannot bill you again without you buying again. When you do choose to renew, this policy applies to that purchase exactly as it does to a first one.

founder.photoAlt: Paul at Urban Locavore, his Perth shop
founder.photoCaption: Urban Locavore, Perth — the store that started it all
founder.intro: Hi — I'm Paul. I built WCPOS.
founder.p1: That's me, back when it all started. I opened Urban Locavore in Perth in December 2011 with hundreds of products already in WooCommerce and no way to sell them at the counter — so I built a register myself. When the shop closed in April 2014, I put it on WordPress.org for anyone who needed it. POS plugins for WooCommerce have come and gone since then. This one hasn't. More than a decade of releases, one developer, still shipping — and the free version is still the real thing: sell, print, stay in sync. It stays free.
founder.p2: Pro is why it's still here. It adds extra tools for running your store — card readers, refunds at the till, end-of-day reports, multi-store — and it funds every release, free ones included. No investors, no acquisition exit waiting. Shopkeepers fund it directly.
founder.p3: And Pro users have a direct line: tell me what your shop needs, and it shapes what I build next.

shortAnswer.title: The short answer
shortAnswer.wcpos: WCPOS runs inside your WordPress site — your sales data never leaves your store, the free version is truly unlimited (products, customers, cash sales — no caps on anything), and paid licenses are one-time payments that keep working even after they expire. Your point of sale can never be switched off.

architecture.title: What is the real difference in architecture?
architecture.intro: Oliver POS is a cloud platform with a WordPress plugin as its connector: your products, orders, and customers sync to Oliver's servers, and the register you operate is Oliver's app talking to Oliver's cloud. WCPOS is the opposite: the register is a local-first client talking directly to your own WooCommerce database. The practical consequences:

dataOwnership.title: Data ownership
dataOwnership.body: With WCPOS, sales data never leaves your server. With Oliver, your store data also lives in their cloud — fine for most shops, a dealbreaker for some: privacy policies, regulated goods, agencies with data-residency commitments.

failureModes.title: Failure modes
failureModes.body: If Oliver's cloud or its sync layer has problems, your register is affected even though your site is up — Oliver's recent WordPress.org reviews describe orders arriving in WooCommerce at zero value and API errors during onboarding. With WCPOS there is no sync layer to break — but your register is only as fast as your hosting. On cheap shared hosting, WCPOS will feel slow; Oliver's cloud register won't care.

longevity.title: Longevity
longevity.body: WCPOS is open source with a lifetime-license option: if the company disappeared tomorrow, your POS keeps working and the code is forkable. If Oliver shut down, the register stops. This is not hypothetical in this category — Oliver's own plugin went roughly a year without updates before development resumed in 2026, and other WooCommerce POS products have been retired outright.

freeTier.title: What does the free plan actually get you?
freeTier.intro: The biggest practical difference, and the one vendor comparisons blur:
freeTier.outro1: Fifty transactions a month is under two sales a day — Oliver's free plan is a trial with no expiry date.
freeTier.outro2: WCPOS's free plugin runs a real store indefinitely: full catalog, unlimited customers and cash sales, thermal receipt printing, offline-first browsing, on every platform.

pricing.title: What does paid actually cost?
pricing.oliver: Oliver (annual billing): Starter $89 per year — 1 outlet, 2 stations, 3 staff. Pro $289 per year — 2 outlets, unlimited stations, 15 staff. Enterprise $489 per year — unlimited. Recurring, one WooCommerce site per license.
pricing.wcpos: WCPOS Pro: $129 — a one-time payment covering one year of updates and priority support. It never auto-renews, and the Pro version keeps working after the year ends — nothing switches off, ever. That is deliberate: renewals have to be earned with updates worth paying for. Or $399 lifetime. Each license covers a domain plus a staging site, with unlimited devices and cashiers. If it doesn’t do what we say it does, we refund you.
pricing.math: At a single outlet Oliver's Starter is cheaper in year one ($89 vs $129). From year two onward the math flips: Oliver keeps billing every year, while a WCPOS lifetime license is $0 from year four even against Oliver's cheapest plan — and $399 total versus $1,467+ for three years of Oliver Enterprise.
pricing.proAdds: Pro adds: multi-store management, card-terminal integrations, coupons, refunds via the POS API, order history, customer management at the register, store-specific pricing, stock and price editing, end-of-day reports, and the extension directory.

ratings.title: What about ratings and support?
ratings.intro: Averages lag reality in both directions — read the recent reviews on both plugins.
ratings.wcpos: WCPOS: 3.7 stars across 81 reviews — 50 five-star and 21 one-star. Most of the one-star reviews date from the pre-rewrite era (2016 to 2022) and the v1.0 launch period in 2023; we keep a public log of what they said and what changed.
ratings.oliver: Oliver: 4.3 stars across 90 reviews, but the most recent reviews (February to May 2026) report orders syncing into WooCommerce at zero value, HTTP 500 errors from Oliver's API during onboarding, and support delays — one reviewer describes a six-week resolution. claims.title: What Oliver's comparison page gets wrong
claims.intro: Oliver publishes its own Oliver-versus-WCPOS pages. Some claims are fair — kiosk mode, hardware, customer display. Several are not:

apps.response: WCPOS ships desktop apps for Windows and macOS today, and iOS and Android apps are available in beta; current versions of all of them are published at updates.wcpos.com.

multiOutlet.response: Multi-store management is a core WCPOS Pro feature: per-store addresses, tax rates, receipt templates, pricing, and authorized users.

payments.response: WCPOS Pro integrates Stripe Terminal, SumUp, PayPal Reader (Zettle), Square Terminal, Mollie Terminal, and Vipps MobilePay, installable one-click from the extension catalog — and because checkout runs through WooCommerce's own payment system, any WooCommerce-compatible gateway can work.

hobbyShops.response: 5,000+ active stores run WCPOS according to WordPress.org — more than six times Oliver's active install count — with over 400,000 downloads since 2014.

singleDev.claim: Single-developer project; updates as the maintainer has time
singleDev.response: The first half is true, and we're not embarrassed by it (see the FAQ). The second half is contradicted by the public release history — compare it with the year-long gap in Oliver's own plugin updates.

wcpos.title: Choose WCPOS if:
wcpos.body: You want your data on your own server, a free tier that runs a real store, one-time pricing instead of a subscription, unlimited devices and cashiers, open source, or processor freedom — any WooCommerce gateway.

oliver.title: Choose Oliver POS if:
oliver.body: You want kiosk or self-checkout, a customer-facing display, vendor-supplied register hardware, or WooCommerce Subscriptions at the register — and you're comfortable with cloud dependency and recurring per-site licensing.

offline.question: Does WCPOS work offline?
offline.answer: WCPOS is offline-first: products, customers, and carts are stored locally, so you can browse the catalog and build sales without a connection, and everything syncs when it returns. Completing checkout and validating coupons require server connectivity. Oliver claims offline transaction queueing with sync on reconnect.

fees.question: Does either POS charge transaction fees?
fees.answer: No — both let you use your own payment processor at your negotiated rates. Unlike Square POS, which requires Square processing, or Jovvie, which adds a 0.5 to 2.5 percent platform fee.

singleDev.question: Is WCPOS really a one-person project?
singleDev.answer: Yes — WCPOS is built by an independent solo developer (with heavy use of AI-assisted development), and it has been shipping since 2014. Judge the model by its output: the release cadence, changelog, and issue tracker are all public at github.com/wcpos. Team size guarantees nothing in this category — Oliver POS advertises a large engineering team and its plugin still went about a year without an update.

subscription.answer: No. $129 is a one-time payment for a year of updates and priority support; it never auto-renews and no card is stored. Pro features keep working after expiry — you just stop receiving new updates until you choose to renew.

expiry.question: What happens when a WCPOS Pro license expires?
expiry.answer: Nothing switches off. The Pro version you have keeps working for as long as you want — your register, your data, every feature. You stop receiving new updates and priority support until you choose to renew. This is deliberate: it means renewals have to be earned with updates worth paying for, and it guarantees your point of sale can never be remotely disabled. With subscription-based POS platforms, paid features stop when payments stop.

trial.question: Can I try both for free?
trial.answer: Yes. WCPOS's free plugin is unlimited, and the full Pro experience is at demo.wcpos.com/pos. Oliver's free plan (20 products and 50 transactions per month) works as a trial.

metadata.title: WCPOS vs Vitepos (2026): An Honest Comparison
metadata.description: WCPOS and Vitepos, two point of sale plugins for WooCommerce, compared by the maker of WCPOS — pricing, offline orders, restaurant modes, apps, card terminals, and when Vitepos is the better choice.

hero.title: WCPOS vs Vitepos
hero.subtitle: WCPOS and Vitepos, by Appsbd, both add a point of sale to your WooCommerce store, and both have a free version on WordPress.org. Vitepos adds restaurant modes, a customer display and an offline order mode; WCPOS adds desktop and mobile apps and a wider choice of card terminals. Here is how they compare, and when Vitepos is the better choice.

shortAnswer.title: The short answer
shortAnswer.wcpos: WCPOS is a free, open-source point of sale plugin for WooCommerce, with no caps on products, orders, or customers. It runs in any modern browser, as desktop apps for Windows and macOS, and as iOS and Android apps (beta), with any WooCommerce payment gateway. WCPOS charges no transaction fees. Pro adds multi-store management and card-terminal integrations for a one-time payment — $129 for a year of updates or $399 lifetime — and keeps working after the year ends.
shortAnswer.vitepos: Vitepos, by Appsbd, is a WooCommerce point of sale plugin with a free version, Vitepos Lite, on WordPress.org. On 2026-10-07, vitepos.com listed Vitepos Pro from $79 for a yearly one-site plan, and a one-site lifetime licence at $299. Vitepos says it keeps processing orders offline and syncs them when the connection returns, and it has grocery and restaurant modes with waiter, kitchen and table management. It runs in a web browser — Vitepos's own blog says it has no dedicated mobile app — and takes terminal payments through Stripe Terminal and Wallee. On WordPress.org it had 1,000+ active installs and a 4.7-star rating from 54 reviews.
